description: Typed MCP server for bounded Pocket ID administration through its supported API.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md documents the project purpose, bounded MCP design, requirements, installation, configuration, compatibility, release model, security behavior and support expectations.
documentation_interface_justification: README.md and docs/tools.md document the complete public MCP tool surface, inputs, destructive confirmation behavior and intentional exclusions.
sites_https_justification: The project homepage, source, issue tracker, release distribution and security-reporting paths are hosted on GitHub over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: Public development discussion and problem reports use GitHub Issues and pull requests, as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.
english_justification: Project documentation, source identifiers and contribution guidance are written in English.
repo_public_justification: The complete maintained source and history are publicly available in the GitHub repository.
repo_track_justification: Git tracks the maintained source, tests, documentation, dependency lock and workflow definitions.
repo_interim_justification: Normal work is integrated through commits and pull requests rather than depending on unpublished local source state.
repo_distributed_justification: The project uses Git, a distributed version-control system.
repo_tagged_justification: Accepted public releases are tagged in Git; current immutable release v0.1.0 identifies its exact source revision.
repo_unique_version_justification: Release versions/tags identify one exact source revision and published release artifacts are checksum-addressable.
repo_release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md and GitHub Releases document release changes and history.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents how to report normal bugs and propose changes through GitHub Issues and pull requests.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues provides the public issue tracker for non-sensitive defects and requests.
report_responses_justification: The project does not promise a formal response-time SLA; inventing one for badge scoring would not improve this single-maintainer project.
enhancement_responses_justification: The project does not promise a formal enhancement-response SLA.
report_archive_justification: GitHub retains public issue and pull-request history for non-sensitive reports.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md directs vulnerabilities to GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting and explicitly warns against public disclosure of sensitive reports.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting provides the documented private reporting channel.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No formal vulnerability response-time SLA is promised; reports are handled through the private security workflow.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: There is no formal public-credit programme for vulnerability reporters.
vulnerability_report_process_2_justifica: SECURITY.md requests actionable private vulnerability details while prohibiting API keys, generated secrets, private endpoints and personal data.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known publicly disclosed unpatched vulnerabilities in the maintained project; dependency, CodeQL and GitHub security findings are reviewed as release/trust gates.
build_justification: The Python package is built with the declared project metadata and locked dependencies; CONTRIBUTING.md documents uv build as the maintained build path.
build_common_tools_justification: Python packaging and uv use standard, publicly documented tooling and configuration.
build_floss_tools_justification: The maintained build/test toolchain is open source.
build_reproducible_justification: Release hardening validates reproducible package builds from the exact source with frozen dependencies before future publication.
build_non_floss_tools_justification: No proprietary build tool is required to build the project.
test_justification: The maintained test suite is run with `uv run --frozen --extra test pytest -q` and is required by repository CI.
test_invocation_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the exact frozen test invocation and build command required for local validation.
test_most_justification: The project has focused behavioral tests but does not currently publish or enforce at least 80% statement/branch coverage. This is a Suggested criterion, so the project does not claim evidence it does not have.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the maintained test/build verification on repository changes, and protected main requires the real CI gate.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states that new behavior and bug fixes should add or update tests where practical and requires the maintained frozen test/build checks before merge.
tests_are_added_justification: Existing tests cover the bounded Pocket ID MCP surface and security-sensitive configuration/secret-file/API behavior; contribution guidance requires tests for changed behavior where practical.
warnings_justification: The project is Python and has no compiler-warning model equivalent to compiled-language builds.
warnings_strict_justification: Not applicable to the project's interpreted Python build model.
know_secure_design_justification: The primary maintainer has previously self-certified this OpenSSF maintainer-knowledge criterion; docs/SECURE-DEVELOPMENT.md records how secure-design principles are applied specifically to Pocket ID MCP.
know_common_errors_justification: The primary maintainer has previously self-certified knowledge of common implementation vulnerability classes; docs/SECURE-DEVELOPMENT.md records the Pocket ID-specific classes and mitigations used in review.
crypto_published_justification: The project does not implement or publish a custom cryptographic protocol or algorithm.
crypto_call_justification: The project does not implement application cryptography as part of its MCP surface; HTTPS/TLS is provided by the Python HTTP stack/platform and Pocket ID remains the authentication authority.
crypto_floss_justification: No project-specific cryptographic implementation is shipped.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project does not choose or manage cryptographic key lengths.
crypto_working_justification: No custom cryptographic algorithm is implemented by the project.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No custom cryptographic primitive or protocol is implemented.
crypto_pfs_justification: Transport security is delegated to HTTPS/TLS endpoints and is not implemented by this MCP server.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The MCP server does not store user passwords.
crypto_random_justification: The MCP server does not generate cryptographic secrets itself. Confidential OIDC client secrets originate from Pocket ID and are written directly to protected mode-0600 files without being returned through MCP.
delivery_mitm_justification: Source, releases and checksums are distributed over GitHub HTTPS; future releases also publish signed GitHub/Sigstore provenance.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Release artifacts include SHA256SUMS, and future release publication is hardened with signed GitHub/Sigstore provenance rather than relying only on unsigned downloads.
vulnerabilities_critical_justification: No known critical vulnerability is currently open in the maintained project; GitHub dependency/security tooling and release checks are part of the maintained review path.
vulnerabilities_high_justification: No known high-severity vulnerability is currently open in the maintained project; GitHub dependency/security tooling and release checks are part of the maintained review path.
vulnerabilities_medium_justification: No known medium-severity vulnerability is currently open in the maintained project; the earlier test-only pytest advisory was fixed before the accepted v0.1.0 release.
vulnerabilities_low_justification: No known low-severity vulnerability is currently open in the maintained project.
static_analysis_justification: GitHub CodeQL scans Python and GitHub Actions, complemented by dependency and secret scanning.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL and GitHub security tooling target common implementation and workflow vulnerability classes relevant to this Python project.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Applicable CodeQL/security findings are treated as repository/release gates and are expected to be resolved rather than knowingly shipped.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs automatically through GitHub's maintained code-scanning setup on repository activity.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The project does not currently use a dedicated fuzzer/property-based dynamic-analysis tool or publish qualifying >=80% branch coverage. This Suggested criterion is intentionally left Unmet rather than adding tooling solely for badge scoring.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: There is no separate dynamic-analysis/assertion-enabled build mode to claim. This is a Suggested criterion and remains explicitly Unmet.
input_validation_justification: MCP inputs are explicitly typed and bounded; operations validate identifiers, names, group restrictions, confirmation values, paths and configured origin constraints before acting.
hardening_justification: The maintained design minimizes attack surface: no raw HTTP tool, no model-visible API keys or generated secrets, bounded origin, protected secret files, explicit destructive confirmations and postcondition verification for restricted-client creation.
hardening_toolchain_justification: Frozen dependency resolution, full-SHA workflow pins, CodeQL, Dependabot, secret scanning/push protection, Scorecard and provenance-backed future releases harden the build and supply-chain path.
hardening_internals_justification: Sensitive values are kept outside model-visible arguments/output, HTTP errors are bounded, generic remote request escape hatches are excluded and security-sensitive mutations verify preconditions/postconditions.
hardening_api_justification: The public MCP interface is deliberately curated and typed, with unsupported high-risk Pocket ID administration surfaces omitted.
hardening_temporary_files_justification: Generated confidential OIDC secrets are written directly to a configured private output directory with exclusive mode-0600 semantics rather than exposed through temporary model-visible content.
hardening_filesystem_justification: API-key and generated-secret file paths are constrained by explicit private-file/directory contracts and security checks rather than unrestricted filesystem access.
hardening_memory_justification: The Python project does not expose a manual memory-management boundary where allocator hardening can be meaningfully configured by this application.
hardening_environment_justification: Secrets are intentionally file-backed rather than passed as model-visible tool inputs; configuration is narrowly defined and documented.
hardening_logging_justification: The security contract prohibits exposing API keys, generated secrets, private endpoints and personal data; error handling is deliberately bounded to avoid sensitive upstream leakage.
hardening_warning_justification: Compiler-warning hardening is not applicable to this interpreted Python package.
hardening_fortify_justification: Compiler FORTIFY-style controls are not applicable to the Python package itself.
hardening_stack_protector_justification: Stack-protector compiler flags are not applicable to the Python package itself.
hardening_pie_justification: PIE compiler/linker controls are not applicable to the Python package itself.
hardening_relro_justification: RELRO linker controls are not applicable to the Python package itself.
hardening_reproducible_justification: Future release preparation includes exact-source verification, frozen dependencies and reproducible double-build validation before publication.
hardening_provenance_justification: Future GitHub releases publish signed GitHub/Sigstore provenance, while accepted release artifacts remain tied to exact source and checksums.
hardening_dependency_justification: Runtime/test dependencies are explicitly declared and locked; Dependabot and GitHub dependency/security tooling monitor updates and advisories.
hardening_dependency_pinning_justificati: uv.lock freezes resolved Python dependencies and GitHub Actions references are pinned to full commit SHAs.
hardening_dependency_updates_justificati: Dependabot is configured for maintained dependency/update paths; dependency changes remain bounded and reviewed.
hardening_release_justification: The current v0.1.0 release is immutable and checksum-verified; future releases use the hardened release workflow with exact-source checks and signed provenance.
hardening_secrets_justification: Production API keys and generated OIDC client secrets are prohibited from source/tests/logs/issues and are handled through protected file boundaries; GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled.
hardening_security_documentation_justifi: SECURITY.md documents private reporting and the public security boundary, while docs/SECURE-DEVELOPMENT.md records secure-design principles and common vulnerability mitigations.
hardening_least_privilege_justification: The MCP surface intentionally omits broad Pocket ID administrative capabilities and relies on Pocket ID as the authorization boundary rather than adding or bypassing application RBAC.
hardening_failure_justification: Security-sensitive operations fail closed on invalid preconditions, group restrictions, confirmation mismatches and postcondition verification; restricted-client creation performs best-effort cleanup if verification fails.
hardening_review_justification: Repository changes use pull requests/CI/security checks and security-sensitive behavior is documented with focused tests and review expectations.
hardening_maintenance_justification: The public repository documents contribution, security, compatibility and release-maintenance expectations for the maintained v0.1.x line.
hardening_external_justification: The project explicitly states it is community maintained, documents its tested Pocket ID compatibility baseline and avoids claiming support for unvalidated upstream behavior.
hardening_user_data_justification: Contribution/security guidance prohibits personal data in issues/tests/logs/commits, and read APIs return only the bounded fields intentionally exposed by the MCP tools.
hardening_destructive_justification: Destructive OIDC client deletion requires the current client name plus explicit confirmation; other mutation tools use typed bounded inputs and postcondition checks where security-relevant.
hardening_network_justification: All Pocket ID API requests are restricted to the configured Pocket ID origin and there is no raw/generic request primitive.
hardening_auth_justification: Authentication remains Pocket ID-owned; the MCP accepts a protected file-backed API key and never returns it through MCP.
hardening_secret_output_justification: Generated confidential OIDC client secrets are written directly to exclusive mode-0600 files in the configured private output directory and are never returned through tool output.
hardening_compatibility_justification: README.md clearly names Pocket ID v2.7.0 as the tested compatibility baseline and does not imply untested newer versions are supported.
hardening_scope_justification: The product has an explicit bounded administration scope and documents intentional exclusions including user mutation, raw HTTP, API-key administration, SCIM, signup-token and app-wide configuration surfaces.
